name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+40 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold near-certain
Rabb's roughly 130-to-1 fundraising edge plus $1.6M in outside support
Polymarket prices the Democratic nominee at 98% to win
Open seat after Evans's retirement, with no polling to flag risk
model.rationale: The district's D+40 lean, Chris Rabb's overwhelming financial advantage over independent Dennis Mahoney, and market pricing near 98 percent all point to an easy Democratic hold despite the open seat and the absence of public polling.
model.watch: With no polls available, only an unexpected scandal or a sudden influx of outside money for Mahoney would warrant revisiting the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Philadelphia's third district is among the most Democratic in Pennsylvania, with a partisan lean of roughly 40 points. Dwight Evans's retirement leaves an open seat, but the Democratic nominee, state Representative Chris Rabb, enters the general election with a commanding financial position: about $1.4 million raised and more than $1.5 million in outside support. His opponent, independent Dennis Mahoney, who effectively stands in for the Republican side, has raised roughly $11,000, with no outside spending reported on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 98 percent. With an electorate this heavily Democratic and an opponent lacking resources, the seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin in November.
